messages.speaker: human
messages.text: cobalt permissions model review today. This must be airtight before we onboard external tenants.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Current state: one admin role per tenant, and our internal ops team can impersonate tenants.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Proposal: split roles into owner, operator, viewer, and require two-person approval for role changes.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Two-person approval sounds heavy. Park the approval part; first fix impersonation: every impersonation must be logged with a reason.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Agreed: impersonation is always logged with a reason string.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: How long do we keep impersonation logs?

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Security log retention is 180 days; compliance confirmed it in the audit.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Found a real bug: the list endpoint leaked other tenants' rows because the filter relied on session context.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Confirmed: it trusted the default tenant context instead of an explicit filter.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: So the invariant is: every query must carry an explicit tenant filter, never rely on ambient context.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Understood: explicit tenant filter on every query, no ambient context.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: I propose we embed the full permission list into the access token claims.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: That makes tokens huge and stale within minutes.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Declined: permissions stay server-side; tokens stay small.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Session review: security asked for shorter sessions. Current default is 30 minutes.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Audit recommends 15 minutes for all tenant sessions.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Agreed, sessions drop to 15 minutes across the board.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: What if we deployed one isolated stack per tenant instead?

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: That is a hundred stacks to babysit. No.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Audit update: all queries now carry explicit tenant filters.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Next: role names. Keep them boring: owner, operator, viewer.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Owner manages billing, operator manages config, viewer is read-only.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Two-person approval for role changes is still parked?

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Parked; revisit once we have ten external tenants.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Permission check load test: 1.2ms p99 per check. Fine.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: @lead please record this as a project rule: every security finding must be triaged within 48 hours.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Recorded: every security finding must be triaged within 48 hours.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Reminder: explicit tenant filter everywhere, no ambient context.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: I will write the permissions onboarding doc.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Include the 180-day log retention in it. And write it summary-first: one paragraph before any tables.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Will do, summary-first.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Thanks, good session.
